title: Original Petition for Personal Injury
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-56789

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF HARRIS COUNTY, TEXAS

JUAN CARLOS MARTINEZ-GONZALEZ, PLAINTIFF,
vs.

BIG TEX CONSTRUCTION LLC, DEFENDANT.

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

COMES NOW, Juan Carlos Martinez-Gonzalez, Plaintiff, complaining of and against Big Tex Construction LLC, Defendant, and for cause of action would show unto the Court as follows:

I. DISCOVERY CONTROL PLAN

Plaintiff intends to conduct discovery under Level 2 of Rule 190 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure. [1]

II. PARTIES AND SERVICE

Plaintiff, Juan Carlos Martinez-Gonzalez, is an individual who resides in Harris County, Texas. His date of birth is March 14, 1980. He may be contacted through his attorney, Emily R. Whitfield, Esq., at 713-555-0198 or at e.whitfield@lawfirmTX.com.

Defendant, Big Tex Construction LLC, is a Texas limited liability company with its principal office at 4500 Katy Freeway, Suite 300, Houston, Texas 77007. Service of process may be had upon its registered agent, John O’Neil, at the same address.

III. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

Jurisdiction is proper in this Court because the amount in controversy exceeds the minimal jurisdictional limits of this Court, and the incident occurred in Harris County. Venue is proper under Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 15.002(a)(1) because all or a substantial part of the events giving rise to the claim occurred in Harris County.

IV. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

On or about August 1, 2024, Plaintiff was lawfully working as a subcontractor at a construction site located at 2300 Memorial Drive, Houston, Harris County, Texas. Defendant was the general contractor. Plaintiff was injured when a heavy steel beam being hoisted by a crane owned and operated by Defendant’s employee, Robert J. Kowalski, fell and struck him. The incident was caused by negligence, including failure to secure the load and failure to maintain a safe workplace.

V. CAUSES OF ACTION

A. Negligence

Defendant, through its employees, agents, and servants, had a duty to exercise ordinary care in the operation of its equipment and the safety of its worksite. Defendant breached that duty, proximately causing Plaintiff’s injuries. See Smith v. ABC Corp., 123 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 2003, no pet.). [2]

B. Negligent Entrustment

In the alternative, Defendant negligently entrusted its crane to an incompetent operator, Robert J. Kowalski, who had a history of safety violations. See Jane Doe v. XYZ Co., 456 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. 2015).

VI. DAMAGES

As a direct and proximate result of the incident, Plaintiff suffered severe bodily injuries, including fractures, contusions, and permanent impairment. He incurred medical expenses in the past and future, lost wages, and loss of earning capacity. Plaintiff seeks damages within the jurisdictional limits of this Court, including exemplary damages due to gross negligence.

VII. REQUEST FOR DISCLOSURE

Pursuant to Rule 194, Plaintiff requests that Defendant disclose the information and materials described in Rule 194.2 within 30 days.

VIII. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays that Defendant be cited to appear and answer, and that upon final hearing, Plaintiff recover judgment for actual damages, exemplary damages, pre-judgment and post-judgment interest, costs of court, and such other relief to which he may be justly entitled.

Respectfully submitted,

_________________________
Emily R. Whitfield, Esq.
State Bar No. 24051234
Attorney for Plaintiff

[1] See Tex. R. Civ. P. 190.3.
[2] Accord, Jones v. Smith, 789 S.W.2d 111 (Tex. App.—Texarkana 1990, writ denied).
public_law: Smith v. ABC Corp., 123 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Houston [1st Dist.] 2003, no pet.)
Jane Doe v. XYZ Co., 456 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. 2015)

title: Original Petition for Breach of Contract
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-10112

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF DALLAS COUNTY, TEXAS

HOUSTON SUPPLY CHAIN INC., PLAINTIFF,
vs.

DALLAS DISTRIBUTION PARTNERS LLC, DEFENDANT.

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Plaintiff, Houston Supply Chain Inc., files this petition against Dallas Distribution Partners LLC, and would respectfully show:

I. PARTIES

Plaintiff, Houston Supply Chain Inc., is a Texas corporation with its principal place of business at 1234 Commerce Street, Dallas, Texas 75201. Plaintiff is represented by attorney William J. O’Brien, whose contact information is 214-555-0147 and w.obrien@legalservices.com.

Defendant, Dallas Distribution Partners LLC, is a Texas limited liability company with its registered agent, Sarah-Jean Kowalczyk, at 5678 Industrial Blvd., Dallas, Texas 75207.

II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

Jurisdiction is proper because the contract at issue was negotiated and performed in Dallas County. Venue is proper in this county under Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 15.035(a).

III. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

On February 15, 2024, the parties entered into a supply agreement (the “Agreement”) for the delivery of goods. Defendant failed to deliver goods as specified, causing Plaintiff to incur additional costs. This is evidenced by email correspondence from defendant’s manager, Michael C. Nguyen, dated April 3, 2024, attached as exhibitJohn Doe[1].

IV. CAUSES OF ACTION

A. Breach of Contract

Defendant’s failure to perform constitutes a material breach. Plaintiff has performed all obligations, except those excused. See Miller v. Smith, 789 S.W.2d 222 (Tex. App.—Dallas 1990, no writ).

B. Quantum Meruit

In the alternative, Plaintiff conferred benefits on Defendant, and Defendant knowingly accepted them, making it inequitable to allow Defendant to retain the benefit without payment.

V. DAMAGES

Plaintiff seeks actual damages of at least $150,000, plus consequential damages, attorney’s fees, costs, and interest.

VI. REQUEST FOR DISCOVERY

Plaintiff requests disclosure per Rule 194.

VII. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays for judgment against Defendant for actual damages, pre- and post-judgment interest, costs, and all other just relief.

Respectfully submitted,

_________________________
William J. O’Brien
State Bar No. 22098765

[1] The email is incorporated by reference as if fully set forth.

title: Original Petition for Divorce
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-23456

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TRAVIS COUNTY, TEXAS

IN THE MATTER OF THE MARRIAGE OF
MARY KATHLEEN O’NEIL AND PETER J. HENDERSON-BROWN

ORIGINAL PETITION FOR DIVORCE

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Comes now, Mary Kathleen O’Neil, Petitioner, and files this Original Petition for Divorce, complaining of Peter J. Henderson-Brown, Respondent, and would show:

I. PARTIES

Petitioner, Mary Kathleen O’Neil, is the spouse of Respondent. Petitioner’s date of birth is July 22, 1985. She resides in Travis County, Texas. Respondent resides in Travis County, Texas.

II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

Petitioner has been a resident of Texas for at least six months and a resident of Travis County for the last 90 days. Venue is proper under Texas Family Code § 6.301.

III. MARRIAGE AND SEPARATION

The parties were married on December 1, 2010, in Austin, Texas. They separated on or about March 15, 2024. The marriage has become insupportable due to discord.

IV. CHILDREN

There are two minor children born of this marriage, ages 8 and 10. Petitioner requests joint managing conservatorship.

V. PROPERTY AND DEBTS

The parties own community property and incur debts. Petitioner asks the Court to divide the estate in a just and right manner.

VI. TEMPORARY ORDERS

Petitioner requests temporary orders regarding spousal support and child support.

VII. REQUEST FOR RELIEF

Petitioner requests the Court to grant the divorce, divide property, and order child support as per guidelines. See Lopez v. Lopez, 311 S.W.3d 23 (Tex. App.—El Paso 2010, no pet.).

VIII. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Petitioner prays that citation be issued, and that upon final hearing, the Court grant the relief requested herein.

Respectfully submitted,

_________________________
Attorney for Petitioner

[1] The Court may take judicial notice of the respondent’s address.

[2] Affidavit attached.

title: Original Petition for Negligence (Slip and Fall)
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-34567

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF BEXAR COUNTY, TEXAS

ROBERTA H. JENKINS-SMITH, PLAINTIFF,
vs.

SAN ANTONIO MALL PROPERTIES, L.P., DEFENDANT.

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Plaintiff, Roberta H. Jenkins-Smith, complains of Defendant, San Antonio Mall Properties, L.P., and alleges:

I. PARTIES

Plaintiff is an individual, born on February 11, 1978, and a resident of San Antonio, Texas. Defendant is a Texas limited partnership doing business in Texas.

II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

Venue is proper in Bexar County under Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code § 15.002(a)(2).

III. FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS

On April 12, 2024, Plaintiff was lawfully on Defendant’s premises, in the food court, when she slipped on a wet floor and fell. The floor was wet due to a leak from the ceiling. Defendant knew or should have known of the condition.

IV. CAUSES OF ACTION

A. Premises Liability

Defendant had actual or constructive notice of the dangerous condition and failed to take reasonable steps to remedy it. See Taylor v. H.E. Butt Grocery Co., 248 S.W.3d 411 (Tex. App.—San Antonio 2007, pet. denied).

B. Negligence

Alternatively, Defendant’s employees were negligent in failing to clean up the spill, inspect the premises, or warn of the hazard.

V. DAMAGES

Plaintiff sustained injuries, including a fractured hip, medical expenses, pain and suffering, and loss of earning capacity.

VI. REQUEST FOR DISCLOSURE

Plaintiff requests disclosure per Rule 194.

VII. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays for judgment for damages, costs, and interest.

Respectfully submitted,

_________________________
Attorney for Plaintiff

[1] Medical records attached.

[2] Photographs of the scene are available.

title: Original Petition for Employment Discrimination
text:
CAUSE NO. 2024-45678

IN THE DISTRICT COURT OF TARRANT COUNTY, TEXAS

DANIELLE R. WHITFIELD, PLAINTIFF,
vs.

FORT WORTH MANUFACTURING INC., DEFENDANT.

ORIGINAL PETITION

TO THE HONORABLE JUDGE OF SAID COURT:

Plaintiff, Danielle R. Whitfield, brings this action against Fort Worth Manufacturing Inc., and states:

I. PARTIES

Plaintiff resides in Tarrant County, Texas. Plaintiff’s date of birth is October 3, 1982. Defendant is a Texas corporation with its registered agent, Thomas Whitfield, at 789 Industrial Drive, Fort Worth, Texas 76102.

II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE

Jurisdiction and venue are proper because the alleged discrimination occurred in Tarrant County.

III. FACTUAL BACKGROUND

Plaintiff was employed by Defendant as a production supervisor. In March 2024, Plaintiff was denied a promotion based on her gender and pregnancy. She filed a charge of discrimination with the EEOC, and received a right-to-sue letter.

IV. CAUSES OF ACTION

A. Gender Discrimination under Texas Labor Code § 21.051

Defendant discriminated against Plaintiff because of sex, in violation of Chapter 21 of the Texas Labor Code.

B. Retaliation

Plaintiff was terminated after complaining about the discrimination, in retaliation for her protected activity. See Perez v. Frito-Lay, Inc., 856 S.W.2d 639 (Tex. App.—Fort Worth 1993, no writ).

V. DAMAGES

Plaintiff seeks back pay, front pay, compensatory damages, punitive damages, and attorney’s fees.

VI. JURY DEMAND

Plaintiff demands a jury trial.

VII. PRAYER

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays for all relief requested herein.

Respectfully submitted,

_________________________
Attorney for Plaintiff

[1] See Texas Labor Code § 21.051.

[2] The right-to-sue letter is attached.
